{{Short description|Finnish mathematician and computer scientist}}
[[File:Jarkko Kari A N Kirillov and Tero Laihonen at University of Turku 20190404.jpg|thumb|Jarkko Kari, Alexander Kirillov and Tero Laihonen, University of Turku, 2019]]

'''Jarkko J. Kari''' is a [[Finland|Finnish]] [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]], known for his contributions to the theory of [[Wang tile]]s and [[cellular automata]].  Kari is currently a professor at the Department of Mathematics, [[University of Turku]].<ref>[http://vanha.math.utu.fi/staff/kari.php Staff profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081205035038/http://vanha.math.utu.fi/staff/kari.php |date=2008-12-05 }}, U. Turku mathematics department, retrieved 2011-09-09.</ref>

==Biography==
Kari received his Ph.D. in 1990 from the University of Turku; his dissertation, supervised by [[Arto Salomaa]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Jarkko Kari|id=20520}}</ref>

He married [[Lila Kari]], a later mathematics student at Turku; they divorced, and afterwards Lila Kari became a professor of [[computer science]] at the [[University of Western Ontario]] in [[Canada]].<ref>{{citation|title=Tytto joka haluaa kaiken|language=Finnish|first=Anna-Liisa|last=Hamalainen|journal=Kodin Kuvalehti|date=December 1992|pages=22–24|url=http://www.csd.uwo.ca/~lila/FinnishInterviewUpdated.pdf}}.</ref>

==Research==
[[File:Wang 13 tiles.svg|thumb|An aperiodic set of 13 [[Wang tile]]s derived from Kari's research]]
[[Wang tile]]s are [[unit square]]s with colored markings on each side; they may be used to [[Tessellation|tesselate]] the plane, but only with tiles that have matching colors on adjoining edges. The problem of determining whether a set of Wang tiles forms a valid tessellation is [[undecidable problem|undecidable]], and its undecidability rests on finding sets of Wang tiles that can only tesselate the plane [[aperiodic tiling|aperiodically]], in such a way that no translation of the plane is a symmetry of the tiling. The first set of aperiodic Wang tiles found, by Robert Berger, had over 20,000 different tiles in it. Kari reduced the size of this set to only 14, by finding a set of tiles that (when used to tile the plane) simulates the construction of a [[Beatty sequence]] by [[Mealy machine]]s.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Kari | first = Jarkko
 | doi = 10.1016/0012-365X(95)00120-L
 | issue = 1–3
 | journal = Discrete Mathematics
 | mr = 1417578
 | pages = 259–264
 | title = A small aperiodic set of Wang tiles
 | volume = 160
 | year = 1996| doi-access = 
 }}.</ref> The same approach was later shown to lead to aperiodic sets of 13 tiles, the minimum known.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Culik | first1 = Karel
 | last2 = Kari | first2 = Jarkko
 | contribution = On aperiodic sets of Wang tiles
 | doi = 10.1007/BFb0052084
 | pages = 153–162
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = [[Lecture Notes in Computer Science]]
 | title = Foundations of Computer Science: Potential — Theory — Cognition
 | volume = 1337
 | year = 1997| isbn = 978-3-540-63746-2
 }}.</ref> Kari has also shown that the Wang tiling problem remains undecidable in the [[hyperbolic geometry#Models of the hyperbolic plane|hyperbolic plane]],<ref>{{citation
 | last = Kari | first = Jarkko
 | contribution = The tiling problem revisited
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-540-74593-8_6
 | pages = 72–79
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = Lecture Notes in Computer Science
 | title = Proceedings of the 5th International Conference on Machines, Computations, and Universality (MCU 2007)
 | volume = 4664
 | year = 2007| isbn = 978-3-540-74592-1
 }}.</ref> and has discovered sets of Wang tiles with additional mathematical properties.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Kari | first1 = J.
 | last2 = Papasoglu | first2 = P.
 | doi = 10.1007/s000390050090
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Geometric and Functional Analysis
 | mr = 1692474
 | pages = 353–369
 | title = Deterministic aperiodic tile sets
 | volume = 9
 | year = 1999}}.</ref>

Kari has also used the Wang tiling problem as the basis of proofs that several algorithmic problems in the theory of [[cellular automata]] are undecidable. In particular, in his thesis research, he showed that it is undecidable to determine whether a given cellular automaton rule in two or more dimensions is [[reversible cellular automaton|reversible]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Kari | first = Jarkko
 | contribution = Reversibility of 2D cellular automata is undecidable
 | doi = 10.1016/0167-2789(90)90195-U
 | issue = 1–3
 | mr = 1094882
 | pages = 379–385
 | series = [[Physica (journal)|Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena]]
 | title = Cellular automata: theory and experiment (Los Alamos, NM, 1989)
 | volume = 45
 | year = 1990}}.</ref> For one-dimensional cellular automata, reversibility is known to be decidable, and Kari has provided tight bounds on the size of the neighborhood needed to simulate the reverse dynamics of reversible one-dimensional automata.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Czeizler | first1 = Eugen
 | last2 = Kari | first2 = Jarkko
 | doi = 10.1016/j.tcs.2007.02.052
 | issue = 1–2
 | journal = [[Theoretical Computer Science (journal)|Theoretical Computer Science]]
 | mr = 2330639
 | pages = 23–36
 | title = A tight linear bound on the synchronization delay of bijective automata
 | volume = 380
 | year = 2007| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref>
